docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

docs.text:
def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:

    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
    except Exception as e:

        return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)

owner, repo = path_parts[0], path_parts[1]

Step 2 — Dynamic Branch Detection (handles multi-segment branch names like feature/foo): 

if len(path_parts) > 2 and 'tree' == path_parts[2]:
    join_parts = lambda i: '/'.join(path_parts[i:])

    # Fetch all branches
    branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches
    branch_names = map(lambda b: b.get("name"), branches)

    # Match URL path against branch names (handles multi-segment names)

    ref = next((name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name)), None)

    # Fallback: check if it's a commit/tree hash

        tree = path_parts[3]
        ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}

    # Extract subdirectory (accounts for multi-slash branch names)
    part_index = 5 if '/' in ref else 4
    specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
else:

    specific_path = ""

Step 3 — Remote .gitignore Fetch: 

gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
if gi_resp.status_code == 200:

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

Notes for AI: Each node handles malformed LLM output differently. This table determines whether a node retries (via PocketFlow's retry mechanism) or silently skips bad items.

Node Validation Style Behavior on Invalid Output FetchRepo Strict Raises ValueError if 0 files crawled ContextRouter N/A Internal math, no LLM output to validate IdentifyAbstractions Strict on structure, lenient on indices Raises ValueError if not list, missing keys, or wrong types → triggers retry. docs.title: 14. Prompt Template Rules
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Prompt templates are in prompts/tutorial/, prompts/advanced/, prompts/api-reference/, and prompts/sdk/. They contain {placeholder} variables that form a CONTRACT with the node code.

  1. NEVER paraphrase, truncate, or summarize prompt templates — copy them byte-for-byte from the originals
  2. The {variable} placeholders are a CONTRACT — nodes MUST pass exactly matching kwargs to .format()
  3. To verify correctness: grep each template for {word} patterns. Every match must appear as a kwarg in the corresponding node's .format() call
  4. Templates use Python .format() syntax — any literal { or } in template text MUST be escaped as {{ or }}
  5. All 4 directories (tutorial/, advanced/, api-reference/, sdk/) have the SAME 6 template files. The tutorial/ and advanced/ directories share identical placeholder names. The api-reference/ and sdk/ templates may have different placeholder sets (e.g., api-reference/draft_chapters.md omits {tone_note}, {chapter_num}, {instruction_lang_note}, {code_comment_note}, {mermaid_lang_note}).

docs.text:
Notes for AI: This is the EXACT content of flow.py. Reproduce it exactly.

from pocketflow import Flow
from nodes import (
    FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions,
    IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters,
    WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, DeterministicFileMapper
)

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

docs.title: flow
docs.text: File Path: flow.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The flow module defines the core directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflow for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder using the pocketflow framework. It configures and links all execution nodes responsible for repository fetching, context routing, abstraction mapping, chapter sequencing, content writing, and tutorial synthesis.

Depending on the context routing strategy selected during execution (direct, batch, or deterministic), the workflow dynamically branches to process codebase contexts of varying sizes before converging to write chapters and assemble the final tutorial.

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Instantiates and configures the pocketflow.Flow computational graph for the tutorial generation pipeline. It initializes all workflow nodes with operational parameters (such as max_retries=5 and wait=20 seconds for LLM-bound operations) and sets up the node routing topology:

  1. Initialization: Creates instances of FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, and DeterministicFileMapper.
  2. Repository Fetch & Routing: Connects FetchRepo to ContextRouter.
  3. Branching Paths:
  4. "direct" route: Routes to IdentifyAbstractions for codebases fitting in single-prompt contexts.
  5. "batch" route: Routes to MapAbstractions followed by ReduceAbstractions for larger multi-batch codebases.
  6. "deterministic" route: Routes to DeterministicFileMapper for file-by-file deterministic chapter mappings.
  7. Synthesis & Convergence:
  8. Connects IdentifyAbstractions and ReduceAbstractions into AnalyzeRelationships.
  9. Connects AnalyzeRelationships to OrderChapters, which leads into WriteChapters.
  10. Connects DeterministicFileMapper directly into WriteChapters.
  11. Routes WriteChapters into CombineTutorial for the final markdown aggregation.

Parameters: None

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow pipeline with FetchRepo configured as the entry point node (start).

Raises: None directly raised during declaration.*

Example: 

from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# Instantiate the pipeline
tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

# Execute the flow with shared context dictionary
shared_context = {
    "repo_path": "https://github.com/example/repo",
    "output_dir": "./output"
}
tutorial_flow.run(shared_context)

Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Executes the top-level CLI workflow for generating codebase documentation and tutorials: 1. Environment Setup: Loads environment variables from .env using dotenv.load_dotenv(). 2. CLI Parsing: Configures and parses command-line arguments using argparse.ArgumentParser. Supports mutually exclusive target source inputs (--repo for remote GitHub repositories or --dir for local paths), output directory selection, pattern filtering, documentation modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), token overrides, caching, and batching limits. 3. Shared Store Instantiation: Constructs the shared dictionary that nodes read from and write to across pipeline execution. 6. Execution Graph: Instantiates the workflow graph using create_tutorial_flow() and executes it against the shared state. 7. Post-execution Cleanup: If the --cleanup flag is set, deletes the llm_cache.json file and removes the configured log directory.

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised by argparse if mandatory arguments (such as --repo or --dir) are missing or if --help is requested. * Exception: May propagate unhandled operational or I/O exceptions during flow execution or cleanup.

docs.title: utils.__init__
docs.text: File Path: utils/__init__.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.__init__ module serves as the package initialization file for the utils package within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder project. It establishes the utils namespace, allowing standard modular imports of utility subsystems across the framework.

The utils package encapsulates support services used by nodes and main, including: * LLM provider communication and context token resolution via utils.call_llm. * Remote Git repository crawling and extraction via utils.crawl_github_files. * Local file system indexing and pattern-based filtering via utils.crawl_local_files. * Token estimation and budget logging helpers via utils.token_utils.

docs.title: Package Exports and Definitions
docs.text: utils/__init__.py does not define or export module-level constants, classes, or helper functions directly. Submodules are imported explicitly across the codebase from their respective module paths.

docs.title: Submodules
docs.text: Submodule Description utils.call_llm Universal LLM interface supporting OpenAI, Azure, Gemini, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and local endpoints. utils.crawl_github_files Fetches and filters repository trees and file contents using GitHub REST API endpoints. utils.crawl_local_files Scans, matches, and reads source files from local directories using glob pattern rules. utils.token_utils Provides token estimation logging and debug output utilities.

docs.title: Example Import Usage
docs.text:
# Direct submodule imports
from utils.call_llm import call_llm, get_model_context_length
from utils.crawl_local_files import crawl_local_files
from utils.crawl_github_files import crawl_github_files
from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation

docs.title: utils.call_llm
docs.text: File Path: utils/call_llm.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.call_llm module provides the unified LLM execution layer for Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. It abstracts downstream model invocations across multiple providers, including native Google Gemini (via the google-genai SDK using either API keys or Google Cloud Vertex AI) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (such as OpenRouter and local Ollama instances).

Key responsibilities include: - Multi-provider routing based on environment configuration (GEMINI, OPENROUTER, OLLAMA). - Simple persistent prompt/response caching via llm_cache.json to prevent duplicate API queries during development and pipeline reruns. - Reasoning effort / thinking budget configuration (e.g., Gemini thinking tokens, OpenRouter reasoning effort, Ollama think parameters). - Dynamic model context window inspection via API querying or provider heuristics. - Structured file logging for all prompt and response payloads under the configured log directory.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum input context window (in tokens) for a specified model and endpoint. Used by main and nodes to calculate safety margins and batch boundaries. - If endpoint_url matches generativelanguage.googleapis.com or model_name contains "gemini", defaults to 1,000,000 tokens. - If endpoint_url contains "openrouter.ai", fetches model details from /api/v1/models and extracts context_length. - Defaults to 100,000 tokens if unknown, empty, or if an error occurs.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Base URL or endpoint of the LLM provider. * model_name (str): Name or ID of the model. * api_key (str, optional): Provider API key. Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: Maximum context length in tokens.

Raises: None* (Catches all exceptions internally and logs a warning).

Example: 

from utils.call_llm import get_model_context_length

context_len = get_model_context_length("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", "openai/gpt-4o")
# Returns context token limit integer

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an LLM inference call against generic OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints (such as OpenRouter or Ollama). Reads target configuration from dynamic environment variables based on LLM_PROVIDER (<provider>_MODEL, <provider>_BASE_URL, <provider>_API_KEY). Appends /v1/chat/completions to the base URL and formats the payload.

Handles extended reasoning configuration when thinking_level is provided: - OpenRouter: Queries _get_openrouter_model_info to verify if the model supports reasoning effort and maps payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()} with temperature 1.0. - Ollama: Populates payload["think"] and payload["reasoning_effort"] with temperature 1.0.

Logs prompts and responses, validates JSON responses, and unwraps the text content from response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].

Parameters: * prompt (str): Prompt text string sent to the LLM. * thinking_level (str, optional): Reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw text content generated by the model.

Raises: * ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, or <provider>_BASE_URL are not set in the environment, or if the server response is invalid JSON. * Exception: On network connection failure, request timeout, HTTP error, or bad status codes.

Example: 

# Assuming LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER, OPENROUTER_MODEL=..., OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=...
from utils.call_llm import _call_llm_provider

response = _call_llm_provider("Explain quicksort in Python", thinking_level="low")

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an inference call against Google Gemini models using the official google-genai SDK. Resolves authentication via Google Cloud Vertex AI (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and optional GEMINI_LOCATION) or standalone API key (GEMINI_API_KEY).

Reads the model from GEMINI_MODEL (defaulting to "gemini-3.7-flash"). When thinking_level is passed, maps the level to explicit token budgets (low -> 1024, medium -> 4096, high -> 8192) and attaches a types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget) to the generation config.

Extracts and concatenates only text content parts from candidate responses to avoid including non-text metadata (such as thought signatures).

Parameters: * prompt (str): Prompt text string sent to the model. * thinking_level (str, optional): Reasoning effort budget level ("low", "medium", or "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Concatenated text response generated by Gemini, or an empty string if no candidate parts are present.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is set in the environment. * Exception: If the Gemini SDK client generation call fails.

Example: 

from utils.call_llm import _call_llm_gemini

response = _call_llm_gemini("Generate an architectural summary", thinking_level="medium")

docs.title: utils.crawl_github_files
docs.text: File Path: utils/crawl_github_files.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module is responsible for ingesting source code and file trees from remote GitHub repositories. It serves as one of the underlying repository-fetching implementations called by the FetchRepo node in the computational flow.

The module provides dual retrieval mechanisms: 1. Git SSH Cloning: For SSH URLs (git@... or URLs ending with .git), the module performs a temporary shallow repository clone using git.Repo.clone_from, scans the directory tree using os.walk, applies inclusion/exclusion filters along with .gitignore patterns via pathspec, and reads file contents directly with utf-8-sig encoding. 2. GitHub REST API Traversal: For standard HTTP/HTTPS URLs, the module parses the repository owner, repository name, branch or tree commit SHA, and subdirectories. It uses the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} and /git/trees/{tree}) to recursively traverse directories, handle rate-limit resets (403/429), parse remote .gitignore files, and fetch content via raw download URLs or base64 decoding.

Both mechanisms enforce file size limits, filter files against glob patterns, skip binary/non-text files, and output ANSI-colored terminal summaries.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url: str, token: str = None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: Union[str, Set[str]] = None, exclude_patterns: Union[str, Set[str]] = None) -> dict:

Description: Crawls files from a specified GitHub repository URL at an optional branch, commit SHA, or subpath. Automatically selects between SSH repository cloning via GitPython and the GitHub REST API depending on the URL schema.

Under the hood: - Normalizes include_patterns and exclude_patterns into sets. - If the URL starts with git@ or ends with .git: - Creates a temporary directory using tempfile.TemporaryDirectory. - Clones the repository using git.Repo.clone_from. - Parses .gitignore using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...) if present. - Recursively traverses the directory tree using os.walk, pruning excluded directories and filtering files via should_include_file. - Enforces max_file_size and reads contents using utf-8-sig. - If the URL is an HTTP/HTTPS GitHub URL: - Parses the URL components (owner, repo, optional branch/tree ref, and subdirectory path). - Fetches branches via fetch_branches or verifies trees via check_tree to resolve tree references and subdirectory paths. - Queries contents/.gitignore via the REST API to construct a pathspec matcher. - Recursively invokes fetch_contents to traverse the repository structure. - Handles API rate-limiting headers (X-RateLimit-Reset), pausing execution when limits are reached if a token is supplied. - Reads text contents via download_url HTTP requests or decodes base64 content payloads. - Prints a color-coded summary to standard output and returns a dictionary containing the path-to-content map and execution statistics.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Target GitHub repository URL (e.g., 'https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/subdir' or 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git'). * token (str | None, optional): GitHub personal access token for authenticating private repositories and raising API rate limits. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum file size in bytes to read into memory. Defaults to 1048576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): If True, returns dictionary keys relative to the specified URL subdirectory rather than repository root. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): File pattern or set of glob patterns to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.md"}). If None, all files are included. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): File pattern or set of glob patterns to exclude (e.g., {"test/*", "*.png"}). If None, no patterns are excluded.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary structured as: - "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of relative file paths to string file contents. - "stats" (dict[str, Any]): Metadata dictionary containing downloaded_count, skipped_count, skipped_files, base_path, include_patterns, exclude_patterns, and optionally source or error.

Raises: * ValueError: If repo_url cannot be parsed into valid GitHub repository components (owner and repository name). * Exception: If GitHub API rate limits are exceeded without a token provided, or if git clone operations fail.

Example: 

from utils.crawl_github_files import crawl_github_files

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url="https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/main/pydantic",
    token="ghp_exampletoken12345",
    max_file_size=512 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True,
    include_patterns={"*.py"},
    exclude_patterns={"tests/*"}
)

files = result["files"]
print(f"Downloaded {len(files)} files.")

Description: Evaluates whether a given file matches the inclusion, exclusion, and .gitignore criteria. 1. Tests file_name against include_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch. If include_patterns is empty, defaults to True. 2. If included and gitignore_spec is provided, tests file_path against gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path); returns False if matched. 3. Returns: * bool: True if the file satisfies all filtering criteria and should be crawled; False otherwise.

Raises: * None

# Internal usage within crawl_github_files
is_valid = should_include_file("src/utils/math.py", "math.py", gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec)

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Internal recursive helper within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively navigates the GitHub repository hierarchy using the REST API GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}: - Appends the query parameter ref if a branch/commit is specified. - If rate-limited (403/429), reads X-RateLimit-Reset, sleeps until the quota resets, and retries the request. - Iterates over items returned in the directory listing: - Directories (dir): Checks gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns. If excluded, prints an ANSI exclusion log; otherwise, recursively calls fetch_contents(item["path"]). - Files (file): Checks patterns via should_include_file and enforces max_file_size. Downloads content using download_url or falls back to decoding base64 payloads from item["url"]. Updates the outer files dictionary and tracking counters.

Parameters: * path (str): Repository directory path to inspect.

Returns: * None (Updates the enclosing files dictionary and counter state in-place).

Raises: * Exception: If GitHub API rate limits are hit without a configured token.

Example: 

# Internal invocation within crawl_github_files
fetch_contents("src/core")

docs.title: utils.crawl_local_files
docs.text: File Path: utils/crawl_local_files.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_local_files module provides local filesystem directory crawling and source ingestion capabilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It is utilized by the FetchRepo node when local directory paths (--dir) are targeted instead of remote Git repositories.

The module mirrors the functional interface and filtering logic of utils.crawl_github_files, enabling uniform downstream processing. It features: - Recursive directory traversal via os.walk with in-place directory pruning to avoid traversing excluded directory branches. - Automatic .gitignore pattern loading and matching using pathspec.PathSpec with gitwildmatch rules. - Glob-based include and exclude pattern filtering using fnmatch. - File size threshold validation to avoid loading large assets into memory. - Safe text decoding with utf-8-sig encoding, filtering out binary and non-text files. - Formatted ANSI terminal summary reporting with detailed metrics on processed, excluded, oversized, and unreadable files.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory: str, include_patterns: set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: set[str] | None = None, max_file_size: int | None = None, use_relative_paths: bool = True) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:

Description: Performs a single-pass traversal of a local directory, applying hierarchical directory pruning, .gitignore rules, inclusion/exclusion wildcard filters, file size limits, and UTF-8 encoding checks.

Under the hood, the function performs the following steps: 1. Validation: Checks if directory exists using os.path.isdir(), raising ValueError if the directory is missing. 2. Gitignore Discovery: Checks for a .gitignore file located directly under directory. If found, parses its lines using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...) with utf-8-sig encoding. If parsing fails, logs a warning and continues without .gitignore filtering. 3. Recursive Traversal & Directory Pruning: - Walks the directory tree using os.walk(directory). - Iterates through subdirectories (dirs), calculating their relative path to directory. - Checks subdirectories against gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns (normalizing trailing /* wildcards). - Dynamically mutates dirs in-place by removing excluded directories, preventing unnecessary recursive traversal into ignored subtrees (such as node_modules, .git, or build caches). - Sorts the remaining dirs in-place for deterministic alphabetical traversal ordering. 4. File Filtering and Ingestion: - Iterates over sorted files within the current directory. - Computes relative paths if use_relative_paths=True, or absolute/verbatim paths otherwise. - Tests relpath against gitignore_spec.match_file(relpath). Skips and logs with ANSI gray if matched. - Tests relpath against exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch. Skips and logs if matched. - Tests relpath against include_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch (if include_patterns is provided). Skips if no pattern matches. - Inspects file size via os.path.getsize(filepath). Skips and logs with ANSI red if max_file_size is exceeded. - Reads text contents using open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig"). - Catches UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError for binary/non-text files and records them in skipped_non_text. - Successfully read files are added to files_dict[relpath]. 5. Summary Reporting: - Prints a formatted terminal summary to standard output detailing total discovered items, processed count, excluded count, oversized files, and unparseable non-text files. 6. Return: Returns a dictionary mapping the "files" key to the populated path-to-content dictionary.

Parameters: * directory (str): Target root filesystem path to crawl. * include_patterns (set[str] | None, optional): Set of wildcard glob patterns to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). If None or empty, all non-excluded files are considered. Defaults to None. * exclude_patterns (set[str] | None, optional): Set of wildcard glob patterns to ignore (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.log"}). Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int | None, optional): Maximum allowable file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. Defaults to None. * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether the dictionary keys should be relative to directory (True) or use full filepath strings (False). Defaults to True.

Returns: * dict[str, dict[str, str]]: A dictionary containing: - "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of relative (or full) file path strings to their decoded file text contents.

Raises: * ValueError: If directory does not exist or is not a valid directory.

Example: 

from utils.crawl_local_files import crawl_local_files

# Crawl a local project folder ignoring caches and tests
result = crawl_local_files(
    directory="./my_project",
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},
    exclude_patterns={"tests/*", "__pycache__/*", "*.pyc"},
    max_file_size=512 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True
)

files = result["files"]
for path, content in files.items():
    print(f"Loaded {path} ({len(content)} characters)")

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.token_utils module provides token counting estimation and command-line analytics logging across the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It is utilized by computational workflow nodes (such as DeterministicFileMapper and prompt-preparation stages) to track prompt sizes and monitor LLM context window utilization in real time.

The module attempts accurate token counting using the tiktoken library with the cl100k_base encoding model. If tiktoken encounters an error or is unavailable, it seamlessly falls back to a 4-characters-per-token heuristic (len(prompt_content) // 4). It formats the resulting token statistics and prints colorized ANSI terminal output indicating the active node, token usage, maximum limit, and context percentage.

docs.title: log_token_estimation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int) -> None:

Description: Estimates the token count for a given prompt string and prints a formatted analytics line to standard output using ANSI yellow terminal styling (\033[93m).

Under the hood: 1. Token Estimation: Attempts to load the cl100k_base tokenizer via tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base") and encodes prompt_content to retrieve the exact token count. 2. Fallback Strategy: If an exception occurs during tokenizer loading or encoding, falls back to an integer division heuristic of len(prompt_content) // 4. 3. Capacity Calculation: Calculates the percentage of total capacity consumed ((token_count / max_tokens) * 100). If max_tokens is 0, defaults capacity to 0. 4. Console Output: Prints a formatted log line in the format: 

[Token Analytics] <node_name>: <token_count> / <max_tokens> tokens (<percentage>% capacity)

Parameters: * node_name (str): The name or identifier of the calling pipeline node (e.g., "DeterministicFileMapper", "IdentifyAbstractions"). * prompt_content (str): The full text of the prompt to be analyzed for token consumption. * max_tokens (int): The maximum context window limit configured for the target model.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None (Catches all exceptions internally during token encoding to execute the fallback calculation).

Example: 

from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation

prompt = "Analyze the architectural structure of the following codebase..."
max_context_limit = 128000

# Logs: [Token Analytics] AbstractionMapper: 14 / 128,000 tokens (0.0% capacity)
log_token_estimation("AbstractionMapper", prompt, max_context_limit)
